title: Where held capacity goes
caption: Llama 3 405B's 16,384 dedicated GPUs for 54 days: scheduling loss vanishes on a dedicated cluster, about a tenth is lost at the runtime boundary, more than half at the program boundary, and roughly 37 percent of held capacity becomes training progress.
alt: Waterfall of Llama 3 held capacity draining through runtime and program boundaries into a 37 percent progress share

title: Runtime loss composition at 128 GPUs
caption: The five additive runtime terms for the 128-GPU example, ranked: input waits outweigh preemption, which outweighs the failure terms — at this scale the input lever is worth roughly ten times the failure lever.
alt: Horizontal bars ranking input waits largest, then preemption, then failure recovery, checkpoint waste and startup for the 128-GPU example

title: Batch-one decode on the roofline
caption: Arithmetic intensity fixes the ceiling: batch-one decode on the 70B replica sits near 1.8 FLOPs per byte, far below the H100 ridge, so even at 84 percent of achievable bandwidth it runs at well under one percent of peak FP16 compute.
alt: Roofline plot with bandwidth ceiling and compute ceiling, decode point far left below the bandwidth roof

title: Trading between factors
caption: A lever that raises one factor and lowers another is judged by the product. For the running example a point of P is worth most, then S, then R — and about a quarter of runtime goodput is what a P lever can afford to give up.
alt: Schematic of the goodput product surface with single-factor optima off the product-maximizing ridge
